findings.statement: Relative to the user anchor date 2026-08-15, “next Friday” is the calendar date 2026-08-21. For an unambiguous, reproducible closing convention for that Friday I will use the CME CF Bitcoin Reference Rate (BRR) published for 21 August 2026 — the BRR is defined as the index representing trade activity during the 60-minute TWAP ending at 16:00 London time on the Calculation Day (disseminated after that time).

CME/CF Benchmarks specify the BRR observation window as the 60-minute TWAP up to and including 16:00 London time on the Calculation Day. In late August the UK observes British Summer Time (BST = UTC+1), so 16:00 London time on 2026-08-21 corresponds to 15:00:00 UTC on 2026-08-21; therefore the BRR observation end (the reference instant for the daily BRR) is 15:00:00 UTC on 2026-08-21. (BRR published daily at about 16:00 London time / shortly thereafter; precision to $0.01.)

Primary authoritative index chosen for the repeatable, reproducible ‘closing print’ is the CME CF Bitcoin Reference Rate (BRR) as published by CF Benchmarks / CME (used for cash-settlement conventions). This index is published at 16:00 London time each Calculation Day and is designed specifically to be a robust daily reference for USD/BTC.

Secondary sources for cross-check and redundancy (to be used for verification of the BRR-based closing print) include: CoinDesk indices (4pm LDN settlement/close convention), exchange daily candle closes (e.g., Binance/major exchange 1d candle close in UTC), aggregated spot pages (CoinMarketCap, CoinGecko), and derivatives market prices (CME listed futures and the CME Bitcoin Friday Futures series). These sources will be used to corroborate the BRR value or to explain any divergence at the BRR observation time.

CME lists Bitcoin Friday Futures with discrete Friday expiries. The listed contract for the Friday expiry 21 Aug 2026 appears as 'AUG 2026 D21' with Globex product code in the BFF (Bitcoin Friday Futures) family — the board shows a contract identifier BFFQ621 for the Aug-21-2026 Friday listing in the CME quotes page. This is the CME Friday-Futures instrument to query for market-implied (tradeable) forward prices that map to the 2026-08-21 settlement window.

CME front-month (classical monthly) Bitcoin futures quotes (example front-month ticker BTCQ6 on CME) were trading in the low-$63k range on mid-August snapshots (CME page examples show BTCQ6 ~ 62,885 in one mid-August snapshot and other front/futures snapshots in the low-63k range). These futures prices provide a market-implied near-term forward context for the 21-Aug observation window (subject to basis, margin, and funding adjustments).

Near the research timestamp (2026-08-15T22:33:03+03:00) two independent spot/aggregate sources reported: CoinGecko live price ≈ $63,486.81 (live snapshot) and Yahoo Finance HISTORICAL data shows BTC-USD daily close for 2026-08-15 as $62,988.45. The difference (~$498–$517 depending on which spot snapshot is compared to which index) illustrates normal cross-source dispersion in spot-level prints vs. index closes. These two independent providers will serve as the live-spot baseline/verification pair for short-term modeling and sanity checks.

A publicly accessible index listing captured during earlier research reports the CME CF BRR value for 2026-08-15 as $62,970.09 — this provides a recent, reproducible BRR prior-close baseline to compare to the spot/futures snapshots when constructing short-term implied forecasts for 2026-08-21.

Crypto options analytics providers and exchanges (Deribit, Pandabull/gvol-style analytics) publish implied-vol surfaces and support deriving implied forward prices for specific expiries. Deribit documents that it derives implied forward prices from option put-call parity (uses options to infer synthetic forwards for dated expiries) and analytics providers (e.g., Pandabull) show an ATM implied volatility for the 21AUG26 options expiry near 24.4% in mid-August snapshots — these resources enable computation of an options-implied forward or a risk-neutral expected price for the BRR observation date using standard put-call parity / forward-implied formulas.

Forecasting approaches available and relevant for producing a reproducible numeric estimate for the 2026-08-21 BRR include: (a) futures-implied forward (use the quoted CME Friday Futures (BFF) or front-month futures and adjust for basis/cost-of-carry); (b) options-implied forward / risk-neutral expectation (use put-call parity across strikes or construct a risk-neutral density from the options surface); (c) short-term quantitative models combining recent spot, futures basis, funding rates, flows and liquidity/volume signals; and (d) consensus/analyst short-term estimates. Put-call parity / Deribit/Derivatives exchange documentation and elementary option-pricing references describe the mechanics for (a)–(b); CME product pages describe how to use the Friday futures series for a tradeable implied forward. The next research step (modeling/estimation) requires selecting one of these approaches and pulling the fresh numerical surface/quotes for the exact Aug-21 expiries (futures quotes for BFFQ621 and options surface for 21AUG26) to compute the implied-forward or model output numerically.

sources.title: CME CF BITCOIN REFERENCE RATE (BRR) Methodology Guide Version: 2
sources.content: BRR.1 Relevant Transaction: Any bitcoin versus U.S. Dollar spot trade that occurs during the TWAP Period on a Constituent Exchange ... Retrieval Time: 4:01 p.m. London time on a given Calculation Day, as given by the server clock of the Calculation Agent. TWAP Period: The 60 minute period up to and including 4:00 p.m. London time on a given Calculation Day. ... The one-hour window is divided into 12 equally-sized time intervals of 5 minutes each. For each partition separately, the volume-weighted median trade price is calculated ... Dissemination Time: Once per day, every day of the year including weekends and holidays, between 4:00 p.m. and 4:30 p.m. London time. Dissemination Precision: 0.01 U.S. Dollars.

sources.title: Mark Prices – Deribit Support
sources.content: Deribit: For dated futures, Deribit enhances the futures order book with implied forward prices derived from options markets. Call and put options at the same strike are combined using put-call parity to infer a synthetic forward price. Multiple strikes are evaluated and the strike with the tightest implied bid-ask spread is selected. The resulting implied bid and ask are added to the futures order book as virtual liquidity. (Describes Deribit's use of option-implied forwards/put-call parity in price discovery.)

sources.title: Inverse Options - Deribit Support
sources.content: Deribit inverse options doc: defines option symbol formats, notes that the forward price for an expiry is the corresponding future's mark price (if no corresponding future, a synthetic future is used), sets out Black-Scholes formula usage for implied volatility and the relationship between options and forward pricing on Deribit.

sources.title: Put–call parity - Investopedia (explanatory reference)
sources.content: Put-call parity is a fundamental relationship that links European call and put prices with the forward (or synthetic forward) on the same underlying, enabling one to compute implied forwards from option prices via call - put + discounted strike = forward. (Provides standard formula and explanation used to construct options-implied forward prices.)

final_answer.answer:
Short answer
I cannot produce a defensible, exact BTC closing price to the cent for “next Friday” (the BRR closing print for 2026-08-21) using only the validated research provided. The research defines the target precisely (CME CF BRR for 21 Aug 2026, observation window ending 16:00 London time = 15:00:00 UTC), identifies the primary and verification data sources, and shows recent mid‑August price context — but it does not include the fresh, time‑stamped market quotes (CME Friday‑Futures BFFQ621 near the settlement time, the 21AUG26 options surface, or spot prints at 15:00 UTC on 2026‑08‑21) needed to compute an exact $0.01‑precision forecast. Without those specific, time‑stamped inputs and a chosen, parameterized forecasting method, an exact numeric prediction would be unsupported by the available evidence. (Sources: cme_brr_methodology_pdf, cfbenchmarks_brr_page, utc_bst_reference.)

(cme_brr_methodology_pdf, cfbenchmarks_brr_page, utc_bst_reference)

- Recent baseline context (mid‑August snapshots from the validated research):
  • CBonds listing of the CME CF BRR on 2026‑08‑15: $62,970.09 (gives the recent BRR baseline). (cbonds_brr_entry)

Why an exact, justified prediction to $0.01 is not provided here
- Missing required fresh quotes: to compute an exact, reproducible BRR estimate you need time‑stamped market data near the BRR observation window (examples: a BFFQ621 futures quote snapshot close to 16:00 London on 2026‑08‑20/21, a full Deribit or other options surface for the 21AUG26 expiry with bid/ask across strikes, and spot/exchange prints at 15:00 UTC on 2026‑08‑21). Without both a chosen method and the fresh quotes, any exact cent‑level claim would be unsupported. (investopedia_put_call_parity, deribit_mark_price_support, cme_brr_methodology_pdf)
